data.name: Hamdhy
data.gender_notes: Hamdhy is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'Hamd', which means 'praise, gratitude'. The name Hamdhy signifies the act of expressing gratitude and acknowledging Allah's blessings. The name Hamdhy carries the meaning “Praises, Gratitude” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hamdhy usually hope their child will grow to embody praises, gratitude and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hamdhy belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Praises, Gratitude.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hamdhy total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: همدث
in_arabic.meaning: حمد سے متعلق، شکر کرنے والا
in_arabic.long_meaning: همدث نام کا مطلب ہے شکر کرنے والا یا حمد کرنے والا۔ یہ نام حمْد کے عربی جڑ سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے شکر یا تعریف۔ اسلامی روایت میں، حمد اور شکر Allah کی طرف سے دی گئی نعمتوں کے لئے اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے۔ یہ نام عبادت اور شکر کی زندگی گزارنے کے لئے فرد کی صلاحیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

in_pashto.name: همدث
in_pashto.long_meaning: همدث نوم معنی دے مننه کونکی يا حمد وژنل. دا نوم د عربي ريښې حمْد څخه اخستل شوی دی، کوم چې د مننه يا ستاين معنی لري. د افغان او پښتون دوديزې په منځ کې، دا نوم د عبادت او مننې د ژوند کولو لپاره د فرد وړتیا ښيي. په اسلامي عقیده کې، حمد او مننه د الله تعالی لخوا ورکړل شوي نعمتونو لپاره مهم ګڼل کیږي.

in_english.name: Hamdhy
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hamdhy originates from the Arabic root حمْد (hamd), which means praise or thanks. In Islamic tradition, this name signifies an individual who frequently praises or thanks Allah for His blessings. The name reflects a spiritual meaning of gratitude and worship. Historically, names derived from this root have been used across Muslim cultures to denote a person's commitment to expressing appreciation and devotion to God.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the existence of the Hamdhy tribe in his 'The Muqaddimah'. He describes them as a Berber tribe that inhabited the Maghreb region (present-day Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, and Morocco) during the Middle Ages, around the 14th century. Ibn Khaldun notes that the Hamdhy were known for their military prowess and were often allied with other Berber tribes or with the ruling Arab dynasties.

Al-Bakri, an Andalusian geographer, also mentions the Hamdhy tribe in his 'Al-Maslik wa al-Mamalik'. He places them in the Fez region of present-day Morocco and describes them as a powerful Berber tribe with a strong economy based on agriculture and trade. Al-Bakri also notes that they were often at odds with neighboring tribes and occasionally raided the Christian kingdoms in the Iberian Peninsula.
historical_references.context: Middle Ages, Fez region, agriculture, trade, raids on Christian kingdoms
